claims.source_span: A DeepSeek Harness extension shows that the effect of an effort-control intervention changes substantially when the harness changes, even when the model, tasks, prompts, and controller logic are held fixed.

claims.claim: The real efficiency metric is cost per successful task, not token count

claims.claim: Token count was the efficiency proxy for coding agents; prompt wording and harness now set the real cost.
claims.summary_span: Token count was the efficiency proxy for coding agents; prompt wording and harness now set the real cost.
claims.source_span: Coding-agent efficiency cannot be characterized by token count or model price alone. We study how end-to-end cost and task success depend jointly on prompt semantics, inference effort, harness policy, model, task difficulty, tool use, context management, and provider accounting.
claims.note: The take's assertion that token count was the old proxy and prompt/harness drive real cost is a supported editorial compression of the source's argument.

claims.claim: Language model agents defeat detectors that look at text or graph structure alone
claims.summary_span: defeating detectors that look at text or graph structure alone
claims.source_span: Text-only detectors that flag semantic drift in review embeddings are blind to graph structure and temporal coordination, while graph-only detectors that exploit neighborhood anomalies cannot reason over review semantics or the cross-modal inconsistencies produced by LLM-generated content.
claims.note: The body's compression accurately captures that text-only and graph-only detectors each fail against LLM-generated attacks.
